label: Week 1
title: FuchAI Intelligent Portfolio
tagline: Where it all began — a portfolio that booted like a desktop OS.
description: Idea52 started here, with a portfolio that refused to be a scroll. The first FuchAI was built as a simulated desktop operating system — a boot sequence, app-style windows, draggable panels, and a desktop you operated like software instead of reading like a webpage. A career, reimagined as an OS. It already carried the seed of everything that followed: an embedded AI assistant, real-time face tracking and gesture recognition that let you steer it without touching the keyboard, and a custom content system — plus the conviction that a portfolio should be something you use, not something you skim. Built in React, TypeScript, Framer Motion, and TensorFlow.js. This was the proof of concept that made the rest of the year possible — and the foundation that, twenty weeks later, would be stripped to the studs and rebuilt into the 3D robot world you're in now (see Week 20).

label: Week 2
title: DreamLens
tagline: A camera that sees your world and reimagines it entirely.
description: DreamLens is a generative camera app with no viewfinder — you point, you shoot, and the AI decides what the world should look like. Every photo is transformed into a completely randomised artistic interpretation: a Ghibli meadow, a Disney frame, a painterly dusk, a comic panel. The model reads the scene — mood, lighting, subject, composition — and picks the style it deems most fitting, not the one you'd expect. No filters. No presets. No control. That's the point. Each shot is a collaboration between what you saw and what the AI dreamed. The output is unpredictable by design — sometimes wistful, sometimes surreal, always surprising. The result is a camera roll that feels like it belongs to someone living seventeen different creative lives at once.

label: Week 3
title: DigitalReda
tagline: Your always-on colleague who never misses a compliance clause.
description: DigitalReda is an AI content writer built specifically for the UAE government digital ecosystem — covering platforms like UAEPASS, Smart Employee, and DubaiNow. Reda isn't a tool; he's a colleague. Friendly, sharp, and quietly meticulous, he knows the writing standards, tone guidelines, and compliance requirements across every major government product so you don't have to memorise them yourself. Drop in a draft and Reda rewrites it to spec. Start from scratch and he scaffolds it for you. He flags what violates guidelines, explains why, and fixes it in the same breath. He adapts to Arabic and English, understands the cultural register of public-facing government communication, and never lets an off-brand sentence slip. The kind of coworker who makes the whole team look better.

label: Week 4
title: Delegation Backoffice Portal
tagline: The control room for every delegation request flowing through UAEPASS.
description: The Delegation Backoffice Portal is an internal operations tool built for the UAEPASS team to manage delegation requests submitted by users across the platform. When a user grants another person the right to act on their behalf — signing documents, accessing services, completing transactions — that request flows into this portal. Operators can review, approve, reject, and track every delegation in the system with full context and history. Designed for scale, it handles high volumes of concurrent requests without losing the auditability that government operations demand. A clean, structured backoffice that brings order to one of UAEPASS's most operationally complex and trust-sensitive user-facing features. Every decision is logged. Nothing slips through.

label: Week 5
title: DropIt
tagline: You didn't just lose weight. You dropped a whole car seat.
description: DropIt reframes your weight loss journey by translating every kilogram shed into something you can actually picture. Lose 5kg and you've dropped a car tyre. Hit 10kg and that's two newborn babies, a medium-sized microwave, or a standard office chair. The numbers on a scale mean very little to the human brain — but holding a mental image of exactly what you've stopped carrying? That lands differently. DropIt makes every milestone feel earned and absurdly tangible. Log your progress and get a fresh batch of real-world comparisons that grow more impressive as you do. Because the best motivation isn't a graph trending downward — it's realising you've been walking around without a bowling ball strapped to you this whole time.

label: Week 6
title: Cyber Gita
tagline: Ancient wisdom. One verse at a time. Keep what speaks to you.
description: Cyber Gita brings the Bhagavad Gita into the scroll age — a gamified card interface that serves one verse at a time, stripped of complexity and dressed in a visual language that feels native to the 21st century. Swipe right on a shloka that resonates and it joins your personal collection, always accessible, never lost. Swipe past and the next truth surfaces. No chapters to navigate, no Sanskrit expertise required — just you and the verse the universe decided you needed today. The Gita has always been about meeting people where they are. Cyber Gita just moves that meeting place to the phone in your pocket. Every liked verse builds into a personal scripture — your own curated edition of one of humanity's oldest living texts.

label: Week 7
title: DubaiNow Service Optimiser
tagline: Find what can be merged, simplified, and streamlined — before users feel the friction.
description: The DubaiNow Service Optimiser analyses the full catalogue of services available on the DubaiNow platform and identifies opportunities for consolidation, merging, and structural simplification. It surfaces services that overlap in purpose, share the same user journey, or create unnecessary navigation complexity — and proposes how they could be combined into cleaner, more intuitive flows. The analysis is visual: an interactive information architecture map that lets teams see the current state and the proposed structure side by side. Spot redundancy at a glance. Drag, reorganise, and refine the IA interactively. When the thinking is done, export the final architecture as a structured file ready to hand off to design and product teams. Less noise. Fewer taps. Better government.

label: Week 8
title: Who Wants to Be a Millionaire
tagline: Built in a cab. Played on the same ride. Finished before home.
description: This one isn't about the product — it's about the moment. Dubai taxis used to have a passenger screen where you could play games on the ride. Who Wants to Be a Millionaire was a favourite for Sayandeep and his wife. Then one day it was gone. On that exact same ride, in the back of the cab, he opened his laptop and built a working version from scratch. By the time they were three streets from home, it was live and they played three full rounds before pulling up to the door. The whole thing took twenty minutes. No brief. No backlog. No approval. Just a problem, a laptop, and the right amount of stubbornness. Proof that the best ideas don't come from sprint planning — they come from missing something so much you just build it, right now, on the move.

label: Week 9
title: Markr.
tagline: Scan the page. Pick up where you left off. Know your books better.
description: Markr. is a smart digital bookmark for people who actually read. Point your camera at any page and the AI identifies the book, recognises where you are, and logs your progress automatically — no manual input, no typing titles, no hunting for ISBNs. Your library builds itself as you read. Every book in your collection comes with a living dashboard: a recap of everything you've covered so far, a spoiler-free look at what's coming, trivia about the book, its author, and the world it was written in. Minimalist by design, obsessive about detail under the hood. Markr. turns every reading session into a richer experience — and makes the act of picking up a book feel like returning to something that already knows you.

label: Week 10
title: Roast My Career
tagline: Your CV walked so this roast could run.
description: Upload your CV or drop your LinkedIn URL and watch an AI roast show script materialise around your entire professional life. The gaps, the vague job titles, the three-month stint you hoped nobody would notice — it finds all of it and turns it into comedy gold. But Roast My Career isn't just mean for sport. Woven between the punchlines are genuine, actionable suggestions: what to reframe, what to cut, what screams "I copy-pasted this from a template in 2019." The format is a full roast script — complete with an MC, crowd reactions, and a redemption arc at the end where you actually come out looking better than when you walked in. Because the best feedback you ever received probably came from someone who wasn't afraid to make you laugh at yourself first.

label: Week 11
title: ZeroEk
tagline: Everything you need to start your business. Nothing you don't.
description: Most entrepreneurs fail not because their idea was bad — but because they never properly validated it. ZeroEk is an AI-driven business validation platform that helps founders stress-test their ideas before they commit. It scores viability dynamically, identifies USPs, maps competitive landscapes, and generates strategic insights tailored to specific market contexts. The result is a clear picture of whether an idea holds up — and exactly how to sharpen it if it doesn't. Built on React and TypeScript with an intuitive step-by-step flow, ZeroEk makes the kind of analysis that used to require consultants or MBAs accessible to any founder with a laptop and an idea. This is going live as a real business. Learn more at zeroek.org.

label: Week 12
title: DubaiNow Redesign
tagline: Every government service you need. One screen that actually makes sense.
description: A ground-up UX redesign of DubaiNow — Dubai's government superapp — built around how residents actually live, not how services are departmentally organised. The redesign surfaces what needs your attention before you go looking for it: overdue bills, expiring documents, pending applications — all prioritised on a single intelligent dashboard. Quick Access puts your most-used services one tap away. An AI search layer understands natural language so you never have to know which department owns which service. My Activity tracks every open transaction across every government entity in real time. A cleaner information architecture, a proactive notification system, and a visual language that finally feels like it belongs in 2026.

label: Week 13
title: Thought of You
tagline: The message you never sent. Finally sent.
description: You think of people all the time. An old friend while hearing a song, a parent while passing their favourite restaurant, a colleague you haven't spoken to in years. The thought is real — but a call feels like too much, a text feels awkward, and so nothing gets sent. On the other side of that silence, someone is wondering if they matter to anyone at all. Thought of You closes that gap with the lowest possible effort. No typing, no composing, no overthinking. Pick a person, pick a pre-written message, and send the one thing that costs nothing but means everything. A gentle ping that says: you crossed my mind today. Because loneliness isn't always the absence of people — it's the absence of being remembered.

label: Week 14
title: Doomsday GPT Drive
tagline: When the internet dies, plug this in.
description: A self-contained USB drive that turns any computer into an offline knowledge fortress. No internet. No cloud. No signal needed. Plug it in and a local website opens instantly — serving the full offline Wikipedia, Stack Overflow archives, satellite and topographic maps, and a curated library of essential survival, medical, and engineering books. Three local LLM models are bundled on the drive, letting you query all of it in plain language. Ask how to purify water, find the nearest high ground, fix a generator, or treat a wound — and get an answer, even when every network on earth is dark. Built for the scenario nobody wants to plan for but everybody should. The ultimate offline brain. Just plug it in.

label: Week 15
title: AI Daily 10
tagline: Ten things about AI. Every day. Always worth your five minutes.
description: AI moves faster than anyone can follow alone. AI Daily 10 is a daily digest that lands in your inbox or feed with exactly ten things — a mix of theory, breakthroughs, model releases, research papers, industry moves, and concepts worth understanding. Some days it's a new architecture explained simply. Other days it's a funding round that changes the landscape, or a concept that reframes how you think about intelligence itself. No bloat, no opinion columns, no hot takes for the sake of them. Just ten sharp, well-chosen items that make you meaningfully more informed about AI than you were yesterday. Curated for curious people who want to stay close to the frontier without drowning in it. Subscribe once. Show up smarter every morning.

label: Week 16
title: Luddprompt
tagline: Write better prompts. Get better answers. Every time.
description: Luddprompt is the Grammarly for prompt writing — a real-time assistant that analyses your prompts as you type and suggests improvements before you hit send. Too vague? It tightens the context. Missing constraints? It flags them. Burying the actual request in three paragraphs of preamble? It restructures. Most people get mediocre AI outputs not because the model is bad but because the prompt was weak — and they never knew it. Luddprompt closes that gap invisibly, sitting between you and any AI tool and quietly making everything you ask sharper, clearer, and more likely to produce exactly what you had in mind. It learns your style over time and gets better as you do. Better prompts. Better outputs. No prompt engineering degree required.

label: Week 17
title: TenderWatch India
tagline: Every government tender that matters to your business. Found before you knew to look.
description: India's government procurement market is worth trillions — and most of it is buried across hundreds of clunky portals, physical notices, and department websites that nobody has time to monitor. TenderWatch India fixes that. Tell the platform what you sell and it does the rest — continuously scraping, analysing, and aggregating government tenders from across the country into a single clean dashboard. AI matches each opportunity to your product category, scores relevance, and surfaces the ones worth your attention. No more missed deadlines. No more manual searching. No more discovering a perfect tender three days after it closed. Built for contractors, vendors, and small businesses who deserve the same procurement intelligence that large enterprises pay consultants for.

label: Week 18
title: MicroKYC
tagline: Verify identity. Share nothing.
description: MicroKYC is a privacy-preserving identity verification ecosystem built on a simple principle: businesses should never need to see your ID to confirm what it says. Users upload their government ID once — AI extracts and securely stores the data server-side. From that point, any business can verify them via email using binary queries: "Is this person 18+?" returns only YES or NO. Never raw data. Never exposed documents. Two live apps power the system — a User Portal for ID registration with AI extraction, and a Verifier Console for businesses running checks with blurred photo confirmation. Every query is logged in a full audit trail. Built on Vercel, Upstash Redis, and Gemini API. Privacy-first identity verification for a world that overshares by default.

label: Week 19
title: Castaway
tagline: Any dumb TV, suddenly a wireless display — no AirPlay, no Chromecast, no cable.
description: There was a TV sitting in the room with no way to wirelessly cast to it — no AirPlay, no Chromecast, no Miracast. A perfectly good screen, marooned. The easy fix is a $40 dongle. The better one was a week of code. Castaway mirrors any screen straight onto that TV's browser using WebRTC — the same peer-to-peer protocol that carries screen sharing on a video call. Open the receiver page on the TV, connect your phone or laptop, and your display is live on the big screen in seconds. No app, no account, no hardware, no cable — just a browser tab on each end and a direct connection between them. It's a small reminder that a lot of the gadgets we're sold are really just a protocol nobody wrapped in a friendly interface yet. So this week, that interface got built.

label: Week 20
title: Outsource the Fight
tagline: Two people, two AIs, one fair verdict.
description: Every couple, every set of flatmates, every pair of co-founders has the same fight on loop — and nobody ever truly wins it. Outsource the Fight settles it. Both people state their side; each side is handed to its own AI advocate that makes the case as hard as it can. The two models go head to head — claims, rebuttals, the works — and then the system weighs both and hands down a single, reasoned verdict. No shouting, no dragging up old scores, no 'you always do this.' Just two cases argued in good faith and one fair ruling at the end. Part conflict resolution, part spectator sport. Built on Next.js and the AI SDK with Vercel's AI Gateway routing the models. Whether you actually accept the verdict is, of course, still entirely up to you.

label: Week 21
title: FuchAI, Reborn
tagline: Tore the whole portfolio down to the studs and rebuilt it as a 3D world.
description: Twenty weeks after it began, the original OS-style FuchAI got torn down and rebuilt from scratch into something far stranger and more alive — the version you're using right now. FuchAI was reborn as a spatial operating system: app-style windows and a full mobile layer, all rendered in real-time 3D. Its new guide is Fuch, a physics-driven robot mascot built in React Three Fiber and Three.js who follows your cursor, reacts to device motion, and walks you through the work. Fuch is also a genuine conversational AI — powered by Gemini and grounded in a knowledge base of Sayandeep's real projects — so you can ask it anything about him and get a real answer, not a canned bio. Behind it, the whole portfolio — every project, every word, the idea52 log — is authored as structured content that ships with the build. React 19, Three.js, Rapier physics, GSAP, WebGPU, haptics. Same idea as Week 0 — just unrecognizable.

label: Week 22
title: Hallucinarium
tagline: A portfolio where every fact is confidently, beautifully made up — on purpose.
description: Every week the internet fills with more AI-written portfolios, bios and case studies — fluent, polished, and quietly fabricated. Hallucinarium is the cautionary exhibit that makes it visible. It's a portfolio where nothing is real: every credential, project and proud achievement is generated live by Claude Haiku and is genuinely, confidently hallucinated. Refresh the page and the lies rewrite themselves — new awards, new clients, new history, all delivered with the unbothered certainty that makes AI hallucination so dangerous. It isn't a bug being shown off; it's the whole point. The piece plants itself exactly where credibility is most assumed — a CV — and quietly asks how you'd ever know the difference. Finalised as a Claude Code build prompt in early June. Satire you can click through, and a small, uncomfortable lesson about trusting anything that simply sounds sure of itself.

label: Week 23
title: Shotcaller
tagline: An AI that takes the wheel of your Canon and calls every shot.
description: Point a Canon EOS RP at a scene and Shotcaller takes over. It tethers to the camera over USB through gphoto2 — the open protocol that exposes shutter, aperture, ISO, focus and live view — and feeds the live frame to a vision model that reads it like a seasoned photographer. It sees the light, the subject and the composition, decides what the shot wants to be, dials in the settings to match, and fires. No menus, no mode dial, no fiddling — just an AI director with full manual control of real glass. Tell it the mood you're after and it shoots toward it; leave it alone and it hunts for the best frame itself. Part autopilot, part photography tutor that shows its reasoning. Built with Claude — proof that 'AI photography' can mean driving a real camera, not just filtering a JPEG.

label: Week 24
title: LiveStack
tagline: Stop your AI coding assistant from coding against last year's docs.
description: Ask Claude, Cursor, ChatGPT or Windsurf to write code and they'll often reach for last year's reality — hallucinated imports, deprecated APIs, dependency versions that haven't been safe in months — because their training data is frozen and mixed. LiveStack is the source of truth that kills that drift. It's a real-time, precision-verified registry mapping the popular libraries across npm, PyPI, Docker and more to their certified stable versions, latest upstream changes, and a known-risk score. For each one it documents the exact 'hallucination vectors' — the specific mistakes models make — alongside the certified correction. Then Context Forge lets you pick your stack and compile it all into a single .skill.md rules file you drop straight into your IDE (.cursorrules, ChatGPT projects, and friends), pinning your assistants to pristine, modern, production-ready standards. Zero drift, no invented APIs — the registry that keeps autonomous coders aligned with the real world. Built with Claude.

label: Week 25
title: Digital Page
tagline: Your neighbourhood print shop, now open online — upload, order, delivered.
description: Every neighbourhood has one — the little print shop where you still have to physically show up, USB stick in hand, just to get a few pages printed. Digital Page drags that shop online. It hands a small local printer a proper storefront: customers upload their documents from home, choose exactly what they want — black and white or colour, single or double sided, copies, binding — pay, and have the finished printouts delivered to their door. The owner gets a clean dashboard of incoming orders instead of a queue at the counter and a pile of WhatsApp messages. No app to build, no website to commission, no technical skill required — just a printer, an internet connection, and suddenly a delivery business. The kind of quietly useful software that doesn't trend on launch day but genuinely changes one small shop's entire week.

label: Week 26
title: Ready
tagline: Stop guessing whether you're interview-ready — measure exactly where you stand, then close the gaps that matter.
description: Ready is a data-analyst interview prepper I built for my wife — so she could walk into interviews knowing, with evidence, that she's ready. Its one rule is honest difficulty: the readiness score never inflates, and only climbs from genuine interview-level answers. It opens with a ~30-minute adaptive baseline across the six domains analysts actually get tested on — SQL, Python/pandas, product analytics, statistics, analytical reasoning, and Power BI — then hands back an honest per-domain profile and the three highest-leverage things to fix first. Every question is generated at runtime, never pulled from a fixed bank, and difficulty climbs as a ladder you earn rung by rung. SQL isn't graded on faith: your query runs in-browser against a real seeded SQLite database and its results are compared to a reference query, so "correct" always means correct. From there it's a full loop — targeted drills on weak spots, timed mock papers under real pressure, and JD-targeted sets that read a job description and build a tailored exam. It all rolls into one overall readiness number, gated behind receipts (breadth, hard-question accuracy, volume, recency) that must all pass before it will call her interview-ready. And because a score that can't be gamed is worth betting on, I pinned real cash milestones to it. Every point is earned.

label: Week 27
title: Papertrail
tagline: A retired Kindle, jailbroken and framed — my live AI ops, glanceable in calm e-ink.
description: Papertrail is my first hardware project: an old Kindle I'd long since retired, jailbroken and stripped down to its bare e-ink panel, then set into a plain wooden frame so it sits on the desk like a framed print. The name fits twice over — e-ink is basically paper, and what it shows is the trail of my own AI usage. What it shows isn't a photo, though — it's a live, always-on operations dashboard of my own AI usage. Tokens burned today across every provider (Claude, Codex, Kimi, Gemini), weekly capacity against each model's limits, a seven-day pulse of activity, the sessions and agents running right now, even the Dubai weather — all rendered in crisp grayscale and quietly refreshed every ten minutes over a read-only cloud relay. E-ink turned out to be the perfect medium: no glow, no notifications, no battery anxiety — just an ambient glance you catch out of the corner of your eye, the way you'd read a wall clock. It's dead hardware brought back as a calm, glanceable window onto the machines I talk to all day — and my first real step off the screen and into the physical world.
